cells: BlueDogDesignDecisions::sizingBaseline
Use the fixed-camber rotating-mast wing as the first numerical sizing baseline; no final sail downselect.
Comparable both-tack polars, wet-cycle durability, actuator energy, mass/CG and dynamic recovery evidence for the alternatives.
BlueDogDesignDecisions

The existing manufacturing CAD supplies a measured section and a practical starting geometry. This enables coupled sizing while preserving the tail-controlled wing and soft sail as equal development contenders for the finite Gorge mission. Availability of CAD is not proof of superior sailing performance.
The source CAD is a manufacturing prototype, not the challenge vessel; the rectangular VSP wing uses its complete midspan section rather than reproducing its swept planform.
BlueDogDesignDecisions::holdingDrive
Evaluate non-backdrivable gearing as an option, not a selected or qualified component.
Motor-off holding under shock, wear, temperature and lubrication changes; moving efficiency, controller demand, jam and power-loss recovery tests.
BlueDogDesignDecisions

Zero motor holding current can reduce finite mission energy consumption, but gear friction and trim movement still consume energy. A locked gearbox retains the last mast angle and requires explicit storm and capsize assessment.
BlueDogDesignDecisions::aerodynamicScope
Use restricted attached-flow VSPAERO sensitivity evidence with conservative sizing assumptions and separate actuator-moment uncertainty; no measured polar is available for this CAD.
Low-Reynolds-number viscous drag, stall, broadside response, thickness sensitivity and both-tack moment measurements; converged heel/wind/trim response across the sizing grid.
BlueDogDesignDecisions

Potential-flow interpolation is suitable for a provisional force-balance model. Mesh convergence and direct candidate checks establish numerical consistency only. Rounded section ends and assumed wake attachment require physical validation; square-sail/downwind performance is not established by VLM.
BlueDogDesignDecisions::structuralScope
Credit finite glass/epoxy laminate sections for bending; give printed substrate no bending-strength credit.
Wet/jointed coupon strength and stiffness, glass-to-print bonds, ribs, attachments, fatigue, buckling and impact tests.
BlueDogDesignDecisions

Thin-wall inertia exceeded the solid-section bound in an earlier sizing trial. Polygon offsets now define finite-thickness section properties. Printed walls/ribs, seams and finish still contribute mass; preliminary material targets are not measured properties.
BlueDogDesignDecisions::recoveryScope
Treat static full-roll restoring curves as screening evidence, separate from dynamic self-righting.
Dynamic releases, pitch stability, ingress/drainage, control restoration and credible failure-state geometry.
BlueDogDesignDecisions

Positive sampled roll moments on a pitch-unstable equilibrium branch do not establish a recovery trajectory. Freely flooded material and fully retained water are distinct static sensitivities, not leakage or slosh predictions.
BlueDogDesignDecisions::energyEvidenceAcceptance
Set evidenceAccepted only after review of evidence for the same installed configuration.

Non-overlapping installed-load coverage; measured power and duty bounds that preserve required functions; installed harvester route/season bounds including outages; temperature/end-of-service battery limits; conservative initial energy; consistent stored-energy and bus boundaries; interval resolution, uncertainty, repeat-cycle phase, source identifiers, configuration revision and review disposition.
BlueDogDesignDecisions

A review Boolean does not automatically audit the records. Recovery demand is a battery withdrawal rate and its reserve stays inside usable capacity. Saving power by violating navigation, collision assessment, signaling, logging or communications does not establish sustained operation. A finite synthetic campaign cannot establish indefinite service.
BlueDogDesignDecisions::uncertaintyPolicy
Separate nominal feasibility, adverse engineering sensitivities and physical qualification.
Measured uncertainty bounds and environmental exposure; hardware packaging/CG; robust feasibility with sufficient mission margins.
BlueDogDesignDecisions

The size search is local and its variable brackets are numerical or model-domain limits. Mesh reserves are numerical allowances, not engineering safety factors. Sensitivity cases are not probabilities. Failed local operating solves do not prove physical impossibility or global infeasibility.
BlueDogDesignDecisions::trafficCourtesy

Prefer safe, rule-consistent routes, operating windows and trajectories that reduce the likelihood of crewed vessels needing to maneuver. Accept delay or reduced mission progress to avoid developing encounters. Once encounter duties apply, preserve required predictable behavior and act when permitted or necessary; this is not an always-yield policy.

Compare alternatives against the same traffic scenarios using close-encounter exposure, predicted need for other-vessel action and mission delay, with explicit behavior and sensing assumptions. These are comparative design measures, not evidence of why another skipper acted or challenge pass/fail criteria. The preference is not yet implemented as a planner objective or validated by the existing replay.

Installed class-specific observations and achieved responses; configuration-specific rule review and recorded authority.

BlueDogRequirementDecisions::recoveryAcceptance
Establish independent course-wide recovery and physical retrieval.
Surveyed accessible shores, final capture/retention, casualty propulsion, onboard observations/control and protected power under no-contact faults.

BlueDogRequirementDecisions::structuralQualification
Accept actual structural loads and installed functional limits.
Wet and aged production materials/joints, impact/fatigue/buckling and combined environmental load evidence.

BlueDogRequirementDecisions::installedControlEvidence
Connect supplied observations and commands to installed sensing and achieved motion.

Establish an integrated acceptance argument beyond sampled predicates and supplied Booleans.
Compatible configuration-specific whole-route, safety, energy, structural and casualty evidence with justified coverage and exclusions.

Select independently scoped future voyage targets and acceptance.
Hawaii route, weather, ocean exposure, sustained energy, communications, maintenance and recovery decisions.

BlueDogRequirementBasis::materials
10 GPa and 50 MPa remain unverified numerical inputs. Qualification may credit only supported wet/jointed material bounds; resize for measured properties.
Directional production coupons, exposure, joint/process variability and conservative allowable/stiffness bounds.
BlueDogRequirementBasis
BlueDogRequirementBasis::structuralScreens
Keep the numerical screening policy explicit: 2/0.5/1 percent deflection, 10 kPa pressure, 100 N proof probe, 50 mm freeboard and 100 percent intact reserve are provisional study controls.
Mission load cases, deformed-foil/control and sealing/clearance sensitivity, attachment loads and casualty flotation. Screen passes do not close these requirements.
BlueDogRequirementBasis
BlueDogRequirementBasis::manufactureAndSites
250 mm print jobs and one-person handling remain owner constraints. A 230 mm tile and a 1.5 m launch depth with 0.3 m clearance are changeable analysis assumptions.
Sliced job envelopes including supports and actual site/depth/appendage clearance evidence.
BlueDogRequirementBasis
BlueDogRequirementBasis::aging
Accept aged material against the capacity credited to the design, not 80 percent of an unaged coupon. Establish mission-representative exposure; 300 MJ/m2 was an unvalidated accelerated-test dose.
Exposure equivalence and aged production-component load bounds; no relative-retention target substitutes for structural adequacy.

BlueDogRequirementBasis::retainedAllocations

Retain safety behavior, environmental qualification profiles, sensing/control timing and accuracy, handling targets and the provisional mission-reliability objective. These are performance allocations, not material or architecture mandates.
Validation of the allocated numbers against handling, control sensitivity and mission/encounter analysis; they are not uniquely derived by arithmetic from the challenge.
BlueDogRequirementBasis
BlueDogRequirementBasis::recoveryStrategy
Treat passive self-righting as a selected vehicle strategy. The Gorge challenge also admits demonstrated autonomous limp recovery after abort.
Concept-specific capsize and shore-recovery demonstrations, including impaired equipment; retain current numerical recovery screens without claiming universal necessity.

Common finite Gorge traffic scenarios; planner preference not yet implemented or validated.
Project owner
Navigation duties, predictable required behavior, collision safety and permitted interventions.
Compare close encounters, predicted other-vessel action and mission delay; no inference about another skipper's motives.
Changed traffic/rule context, sensing/planning capability or contrary encounter evidence.

Prefer safe, rule-consistent routes, operating windows and trajectories that reduce the likelihood of crewed vessels needing to maneuver. Accept delay or reduced mission progress to avoid developing encounters. Once encounter duties apply, preserve required predictable behavior and act when permitted or necessary; this is not an always-yield policy.

Compare alternatives against the same traffic scenarios using close-encounter exposure, predicted need for other-vessel action and mission delay, with explicit behavior and sensing assumptions. These are comparative design measures, not evidence of why another skipper acted or challenge pass/fail criteria. The preference is not yet implemented as a planner objective or validated by the existing replay.
